analysis:
Reviewed all three primary analyses against the replayed workflow patch, documentation patch and changelog. The executable change adds DARKBLOOM_RELEASE_ENVIRONMENT=prod to qualify-sdk (.github/workflows/release-provider.yml, head:239–242). Build-provider retains the resolved release environment; its changed comment at head:181–182 explains the distinction. docs/operations/provider-release.md:315–318 and changelog.d/qualify-sdk-prod-identity.md:3 document production-default qualification on dev branches.
No independently supported regression was identified. Selecting production compile defaults for tests does not itself grant credentials, approve an artifact or authorize serving. The change has no visible effect on prompt encryption, cache isolation, billing, logout, local hold admission or privileged-helper authority. The relevant security contract is exact-build qualification (A-011, A-017, T-054), distinct from serving authorization under TB-011/T-052 and runtime secrecy under T-056.
The local reviews converge on one unresolved integration question: whether provider-release-build's environment input overrides the new job variable, and whether production-default qualification adequately covers environment-specific identities in the separately built dev artifact. Review .github/actions/provider-release-build and provider-swift/Package.swift to resolve precedence and qualification coverage. Their implementations are not supplied; neither a bypass nor complete isolation is established. Replay is incomplete (six reviewed units omitted), so the unchanged signing, smoke and publication controls described in the prior analyses could not all be independently rechecked here. This is a bounded review, not a full audit or deployment qualification.
